items.title: CRM route authentication
items.assessment: The audit claim is stale. CRM pages and server actions use Basic Auth and production fails closed.

evidence.observation: The proxy protects application routes and excludes only required static assets.
Server actions independently require the configured Authorization header.
Anonymous requests returned 401 on 2026-09-13.

items.closureRequirement: Task 4 should verify coverage and close without replacing Basic Auth unless the owner rejects it.

items.title: Persistent idempotency
items.assessment: The header is syntax-checked but is not stored, fingerprinted, or used to suppress a replay.

evidence.observation: Validation ends after checking key syntax.
Each accepted call creates a new random request ID and runs persistence and Telegram delivery.

items.closureRequirement: Task 5 must implement PostgreSQL-backed concurrency-safe replay semantics.

items.title: Distributed rate limiting
items.assessment: The guard works inside one process but counters are not shared across serverless instances.

evidence.observation: A module-local Map owns all counters.
Platform-wide abuse protection remains part of open P0-CONTACT.

items.closureRequirement: Task 6 requires an approved distributed store or platform control and a trusted client-address model.

items.title: Quantity lost by slug deduplication
items.assessment: The selected slug list is unique by design, while quantities are carried separately in items and persist through CRM.

evidence.observation: The contract supports items with integer quantity 1 through 99.
The form has quantity controls and submits items.
Quantity is mapped into persisted order items.

items.closureRequirement: Task 9 should regression-test end-to-end quantity parity and close without redesign if it passes.

items.title: Prisma singleton and pooling
items.assessment: The audit overstates failure: CRM UI already uses globalThis and production uses pooled/direct URLs, but the application service owns a second module singleton.

evidence.observation: The CRM UI uses the globalThis pattern.
Application persistence creates a separate module-level client.
Runtime and migration URLs are separated.

items.closureRequirement: Task 10 should measure actual client ownership and consolidate only if it improves the current boundary.

items.title: Database enums for order type and status
items.assessment: Application types are constrained in TypeScript and Zod, but PostgreSQL accepts arbitrary strings.

evidence.observation: Order.type and Order.status are String fields.
Runtime UI constants provide only application-level constraints.

items.closureRequirement: Task 11 needs a value audit, reversible migration, compatibility deployment order, and rollback rehearsal.

items.title: Client UPSERT overwrites canonical profile
items.assessment: Every repeated phone updates name, email, and region without preserving submitted-versus-canonical history.

evidence.observation: Client upsert overwrites profile fields on every application.
Client has no profile revision or audit model.

items.closureRequirement: Task 12 requires an owner-approved canonical-data and history policy.

items.title: Maximum appointment horizon
items.assessment: Past dates are rejected, but no maximum future date exists for consultations or masterclasses.

evidence.observation: Validation checks calendar validity and the lower time boundary only.

items.closureRequirement: Task 13 must first obtain approved horizons and timezone boundary rules.

items.title: Structured Telegram status references
items.assessment: Orders are linked to telegramMessageId, but the handler still requires a recognizable status line before updating the database.

evidence.observation: Telegram message ID is persisted and used to locate an order.
replaceAnyStatus must succeed before the DB update executes.

items.closureRequirement: Task 14 should make message wording presentation-only while preserving exact order identity.

items.title: Quantity-aware selection
items.assessment: SelectionContext persists unique slugs, while the contact form adds non-persistent per-product quantities. Ordering is accurate, but quantity is not part of the saved selection model.

evidence.observation: Saved selection remains string[].
Quantity is available and submitted from the form.

items.closureRequirement: Task 9 must decide whether persisted selection quantities are necessary after verifying the current user flow.

items.title: Truthful popularity ranking
items.assessment: The visible popularity sort uses static JSON rank without an approved demand source.

evidence.observation: popular compares static popularityRank.
P1-RANKING remains open.

items.closureRequirement: Task 19 needs an owner-approved label and source before Task 20 can automate sales-based ranking.

items.title: Fuzzy catalogue search
items.assessment: Search uses normalized substring matching and has no typo-distance behavior. This is an optional improvement, not a defect without real failed-query evidence.

evidence.observation: Matching ends with normalized includes checks.

items.closureRequirement: Task 21 should start from measured RU/RO query misses and avoid a heavy dependency.

items.title: UTM capture and trust model
items.assessment: The desired URL-to-session capture already exists. UTM still travels in the request body, which is normal untrusted attribution data but lacks explicit semantics and normalization policy.

evidence.observation: UTM capture runs at application startup.
Captured UTM and entry data are attached automatically.
Server accepts bounded UTM strings as untrusted input.

items.closureRequirement: Task 16 should define attribution semantics; UTM must never become authorization input.

items.title: Delivery monitoring and retry
items.assessment: The audit premise that Telegram failure loses the application is false: the CRM record is written first. Monitoring, an outbox, and automatic retry are still absent.

evidence.observation: DB persistence precedes Telegram; DB failure skips Telegram.
Telegram failure returns DELIVERY_FAILED with the persisted request ID.

items.closureRequirement: Task 8 covers alerts; Task 15 separately covers a durable outbox after provider approval.

items.title: Extended CRM results
items.assessment: Revenue, profit, AOV, conversion, regions, forecasts, and comparisons already exist. Reliable processing-time metrics need status-history timestamps that the current model does not store.

evidence.observation: Current analytics include financial summaries, forecasts, regions, and recommendations.
Dashboard includes conversion, regions, sources, products, and time series.
Order has only createdAt and updatedAt, not transition history.

items.closureRequirement: Task 22 must freeze formulas and add status history before claiming processing-time accuracy.

items.title: Telegram webhook chat verification
items.assessment: Webhook secret is required, but message.chat.id is not compared with TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID before mutation.

evidence.observation: Environment includes bot token and webhook secret only; incoming chatId is used directly.
TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID already exists in the application environment contract.

items.closureRequirement: Task 7 should add validated chat identity and negative tests without exposing the identifier.

items.title: Consultation slot management
items.assessment: The current form records a preferred date and time and explicitly avoids promising confirmation. There is no availability or slot model.

evidence.observation: Consultation date and time are preference inputs.
Order stores event strings but no ConsultationSlot relation.

items.closureRequirement: Task 24 starts only after schedule, capacity, cancellation, and API approval.

items.title: Customer status notifications
items.assessment: No SMS, WhatsApp, or Viber provider is configured; this is a new external communication channel.

evidence.observation: Telegram is the only delivery provider type.

items.closureRequirement: Task 25 requires provider, consent, cost, privacy, and RU/RO template approval.

items.title: Operational dashboard
items.assessment: A substantial dashboard already exists with periods, status counts, time series, regions, sources, and products. SLA aging and approved live semantics are missing.

evidence.observation: The deployed dashboard renders current operational and analytical widgets.
Orders refresh periodically and on user actions.

items.closureRequirement: Task 17 should add only approved SLA indicators; WebSockets require measured need.

items.title: Repeat-client history and profile intelligence
items.assessment: Client history, counts, totals, and previous orders already exist. Tags, preferences, notes, and profile-change history do not.

evidence.observation: Client view includes order history, order count, dates, and total value.
Desktop and mobile client detail views render the history.

items.closureRequirement: Task 26 must depend on the canonical profile policy from Task 12.

items.title: Masterclass workflow
items.assessment: The audit is stale about absence: public RU/RO forms, validation, CRM persistence, Telegram formatting, and CRM display already support masterclass requests. A separate published schedule does not exist.

evidence.observation: The public form implements masterclass requests in both locales.
CRM persists and formats masterclass fields.

items.closureRequirement: Task 27 should first decide whether a separate page and schedule add real value.

items.title: Regional customer experience
items.assessment: The shared Moldova region dropdown and RU/RO labels already replace free text. Office, distributor, delivery-time, and regional-manager personalization need verified source data.

evidence.observation: The form renders a shared region select with Romanian labels.
The server accepts only shared Moldova regions.

items.closureRequirement: Task 28 cannot publish regional promises or contacts without approved data.

items.title: CRM exports
items.assessment: No controlled CSV or PDF export workflow exists. This would create a new personal-data egress surface.

evidence.observation: Current routes contain dashboard, results, orders, clients, and catalogue views but no export handler.

items.closureRequirement: Task 23 requires approved roles, columns, retention, audit logging, and spreadsheet-injection controls.

items.title: Telegram bot CRM commands
items.assessment: The webhook recognizes reply keywords for status changes but has no /today, /pending, /stats, or /client command surface.

evidence.observation: Only status keyword replies are handled.

items.closureRequirement: Task 18 requires role, chat, privacy, rate-limit, and audit decisions.

items.title: CRM-to-catalogue popularity loop
items.assessment: CRM has aggregate product sales data, but no approved export, formula, schedule, or catalogue sync exists.

evidence.observation: CRM calculates top products from completed sales.
Catalogue still reads static ranks.

items.closureRequirement: Task 20 depends on Task 19 approving the public meaning of popularity.

items.title: Shared package or equivalent contract architecture
items.assessment: The audit overstates five active duplicates because Telegram and persistence code now live in CRM. Shared schema and constants are duplicated with equivalent semantics, so drift risk remains but a package is not automatically justified.

evidence.observation: Catalogue owns a formatting-different but semantically equivalent schema copy.
CRM owns the paired schema copy.
Catalogue application endpoint is now a thin CRM proxy, not a Telegram service fork.

items.closureRequirement: Task 29 must compare package, generated contract, CI comparison, and repository coupling before selecting an architecture.
